extracted.intended_audience: Small business applicants to NIH SBIR/STTR (R43/R44), biotech startup PD/PIs preparing a Phase I application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling an NIH SBIR (R43/R44) Phase I grant application for a biotechnology diagnostic project, including SF424 forms, project narrative, facilities/equipment descriptions, biosketches, human subjects/select-agent justification, and authentication plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424 Certifications and Assurances (signature requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications* and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances* and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award. I am aware that any false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or claims may subject me to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties. (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must check the agreement box and provide the signature/date of the Authorized Representative. The list of certifications and assurances, or a site where to obtain it, is contained in the FOA or agency-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Are Human Subjects Involved? — applicant must indicate Yes or No and, if Yes, provide whether the project is Exempt from Federal regulations, the exemption number(s) if applicable, IRB approval date, and Human Subject Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Human Subjects are involved, complete associated human subjects and clinical trials information per PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials policies. If No, mark accordingly. Provide documentation of IRB review or justification for exemption where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 4 justification for use of existing specimens/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption 4: claiming exemption because (a) the specimens/data were not collected specifically for the research through an interaction or intervention with a living person, and (b) the investigators cannot 'readily ascertain' the identity of the individual who provided the specimen/data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide 'Exemption 4 Justification' explaining that specimens are completely devoid of identifiers and that investigators cannot identify subjects; state sources (e.g., research partners like FIND) and confirm no identifying information will be provided. If using commercial sera, confirm privacy protections and no identifying information will be shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research — exclusion criteria for non-viable select agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Select agent regulations exclude 'Non-viable select agents or nontoxic select toxins' from the select agent regulations (citing 42 CFR §§ 73.3, 73.4; 9 CFR §§ 121.3, 121.4; 7 CFR § 331.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If work will be exclusively with inactivated, purified viral RNA (non-viable material), inactivation must be certified by commercial vendors or partners. Document the certification and the sources of purified nucleic acids; explain that such reagents can be handled under BSL-1 conditions and list any select-agent nucleic acids to be used along with suppliers and intended biosafety handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources — requirement and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must ensure the identity and validity of key biological and chemical resources used in the study because unreliable or misidentified resources can negate reproducibility and derail research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe general practices to authenticate resources: vendor specification sheets may be accepted, but investigators should independently verify identity/activity before use (e.g., assay new lot vs previous lot). Products used long-term should be assessed regularly. Authentication plans should be based on accepted practices and include specific methods per resource class (see items below). State intention to communicate with community for updated guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources requiring authentication (explicit list)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of resource classes to be authenticated: 1) Linear oligonucleotides for probe-based qPCR (primers and fluorescently labeled probes); 2) Synthetic DNA fragments; 3) Real-time PCR reaction buffer (including DNA polymerase and additives); 4) Purified genomic RNA of Lassa and purified RNA/DNA of other pathogens; 5) Ribonucleotides and T7 RNA Polymerase; (also chemicals like ethanol and fluorophores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each class, state vendor source, provide product specification sheets, and describe how identity/activity will be verified prior to use and periodically thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication methods by resource type (detailed examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to authenticate specific resource types: oligonucleotides — commercially manufactured under GMP with product specification sheets including analytical mass spectrophotometry; synthetic DNA fragments — bulk sequence-controlled before shipment (e.g., GeneArt); PCR buffers — vendor QC plus in-house lot testing as buffer optimization proceeds; purified genomic RNA/DNA — obtain from ATCC/BEI/PHE and perform targeted Sanger sequencing to validate; ribonucleotides/T7 polymerase — obtain from NEB and assess via in vitro transcription, agarose gels and targeted qPCR; fluorophores — validated by wavelength readings; chemicals — supplied with product specification sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the planned QC assays (e.g., Sanger sequencing to verify assay target integrity for LASV RNA, in vitro transcription to confirm enzyme activity) and frequency of verification for long-term lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities & Other Resources section should describe company research facilities (location, shared lab space), central infrastructure (autoclaves, bottle wash, cold storage, BSL rooms), reagent supply programs, basic services (EHS training, permit maintenance, equipment maintenance), office facilities, BSL-2 tissue culture facilities and capability to handle BSL-2+ work, and access to core facilities and partner resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics about the shared lab environment, bench/benchspace availability, biosafety level of spaces, availability of incubators/centrifuges/freezers, reagent programs with suppliers (e.g., Life Technologies, NEB), onsite CRO support, and how these resources will support proposed aims. Document partner core access (e.g., Harvard Medical School Biopolymers Facility) and networking/computational resources including LIMS, backup strategies, and compliance features (e.g., experiment signing, FDA CFR 21 Part 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to external cores and sequencing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should describe access to next-generation sequencing (e.g., Illumina MiSeq) and Sanger sequencing via institutional core facilities or commercial CROs, including quality control steps performed by facility staff and data processing/storage arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether facility staff will run initial QC, where data will be processed (e.g., institutional cluster) and how results are returned; include turnaround times and cost/arrangement details where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment section — instrumentation listing and access
rubrics_metrics.description: List critical instrumentation and direct access to them: e.g., QuantStudio 3/5 instruments, Rotor-Gene Q, QuantStudio 3D Digital PCR System, ProFlex PCR Thermal Cycler, and access to shared/institutional instruments (96- and 384-well blocks, flow cytometers, plate readers, imaging stations, HPLC, Illumina MiSeq, gel boxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify instrument models, how many are available, which are dedicated vs shared, and how they will be used in proposed aims. Describe access arrangements through the shared facility if instruments are not on-site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch format and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biosketch sections shown include Education/Training, Positions and Honors, and Contribution to Science (with examples and relevant publications). Include degree type/year, current position/title, and attach biographical sketch file. Follow page limit and formatting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative attachments required
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract* and Project Narrative* must be attached as separate files (e.g., Abstract_LASV_9-2018.pdf; Project_Narrative_LASV.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure both documents are included in the application and follow FOA/agency formatting/length requirements for abstracts and narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information — required checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must address: vertebrate animals involvement, proprietary/privileged information inclusion, environmental impact, whether site is historic, and international activities/partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No for each and provide explanatory text where required (e.g., environmental assessments, country partners). If proprietary information is included, indicate so. Provide filenames for related attachments (Facilities, Equipment, Bibliography, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent and specificity study documentation (table of reagents and BSL)
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting specificity studies with purified nucleic acid from select agents, list species/material/source and indicate biosafety level for each (e.g., Mopeia Virus — Genomic RNA — PHE — BSL1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table of all purified inactivated reagents to be used, their suppliers, and the biosafety level at which they can be handled. Explain certificates of inactivation and suppliers' certifications to support exclusion from select agent regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner and collaborator resource/support description (Letters of Support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe key partners (e.g., FIND, Bernard-Nocht Institute) and the specific support they will provide such as technical guidance, access to clinical isolates, and support for clinical evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Letters of Support documenting partner commitments (e.g., access to 100+ LASV isolates) and explain how partner resources will be used in Aims (e.g., clinical sensitivity testing, specimen access).
